calls.reason: Karvonen's peer-reviewed study shows a chess-trained model with 99.6% board-probe accuracy, causal interventions and 99.8% legal moves. Acher's o3/o4-mini tests show frequent illegal moves. Mixed evidence on scope.
Acher's May 2025 tests found most o3/o4-mini games ending in clear illegal moves around a median of 15 moves, i.e. by the midgame. The gpt-3.5-instruct exception does not defeat 'often'.
Vafa et al. find incoherent learned maps, which supports the claim. Karvonen's chess model shows a causally used board representation beyond Othello, which cuts against a categorical 'they don't'.
OpenAI's PersonQA results (33–48% hallucination for o3/o4-mini) support unreliable factual use. No evidence addresses whether ChatGPT has a stable internal model, so the claim is only half covered.
